- Termination for convenience: they want the right to terminate with 30 days and prorated refund; they flagged data-transfer obligations and service wind-down.

Diego / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for sending. Attached is a marked-up version of the Order Form (acme_redlines_20260706.docx) — the redlines focus on three practical items: notice timing, termination for convenience, and post-termination obligations. Summary of our asks:

1) Notice window: We are requesting a 60-day written notice to account for procurement/finance cycles. 30 days is tight for us.

2) Termination for convenience: We need the ability to terminate an Order Form for convenience with 30 days' notice and a pro-rated refund for prepaid fees. We do not intend to terminate MSA-level services (e.g., shared platform infra) without coordination.

3) Wind-down/data handover: The Order Form should obligate Redwood to provide an export of customer-owned data and a runbook for transfer (30 days post-termination), with costs capped at a reasonable estimate (e.g., not to exceed one month of fees).

We are happy to align on a longer notice for enterprise commitments — if Redwood can retain a 60-day notice for Enterprise SKU and offer 30-day for consumption or trial SKUs, that could be a path to agreement.

Proposed call slots: Wed 10–11am ET or Thu 2–3pm ET.

Best,
Emily Rose
Sr. Counsel, Acme Labs

Diego / Marissa —

Quick internal note: Legal (Laura + Contracts) will want a consistent approach across Order Forms to limit churn in billing/ops. My initial thoughts:
- We can accept a 60-day notice for Enterprise ARR deals (DL-8921 qualifies) but keep a 30-day window for consumption/short-term pilots.
- Termination for convenience with a prorated refund is acceptable if we exclude non-recurring setup fees and require customers to return committed credits.
- For wind-down, we should offer data export + an export fee schedule (e.g., flat fee up to X tokens or $Y) rather than an uncapped obligations line.

If Legal can get language that: (a) differentiates by SKU/commitment level, and (b) caps wind-down costs, I think Sales can sign off.

Emily — thanks for the redlines and the flexibility suggestion. Draft language below that Legal can use as a starting point. If acceptable, we can fold into the Order Form and share updated PDF before the call.

PROPOSED ORDER FORM LANGUAGE (draft):
1) Term and Renewal: The Order Form term shall be 12 months from Effective Date and shall automatically renew for successive 12-month periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term for Consumption SKUs, and sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term for Enterprise SKUs.

2) Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. In the event Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood will (a) refund any prepaid, unused fees on a pro rata basis, excluding any non-recurring setup fees and third-party pass-through charges, and (b) provide access to an export of Customer data for thirty (30) days after termination.

3) Data Export and Wind-Down Fees: Redwood will provide a data export in common formats at no additional charge for exports up to 250 GB or 1M tokens; beyond that, Redwood may charge a reasonable, documented export fee not to exceed the equivalent of one (1) month of average monthly fees for the terminated Order Form.

If Legal is comfortable with the export thresholds and the explicit SKU differentiation, Sales will confirm the call slot Wed 13 Jul 2026 at 10:00am PT (1:00pm ET). Please confirm DocuSign readiness for the final Order Form after the call.

Thanks,
